summary: Nora now keeps what a group has settled and will need again, such as the wifi password, how a deposit is split or a booking reference, as a memo every room of the group can see and that she reads back when someone asks.
details: Asked to «記低» something about the group, Nora says it will be kept; her background notebook pass keeps it within a few minutes. Something about the speaker alone is still remembered about that person, as before.

A memo keeps what was said exactly as said, a password or a phone number included, and is revised when the group changes it or withdrawn when someone says it no longer holds; earlier versions stay readable.
Each room of the group shows the titles of what is kept, never the values; Nora reads a memo when she needs what it says.
She may also keep something she found herself when someone asks her to keep it.
limitations: A reply still cannot carry a phone number, an id or a key-shaped value, so Nora says such a value is kept rather than quoting it.
Memos are written only when the background notebook pass is switched on.
The memo routing and judgement have not yet been measured against a live model; the labelled cases ship with this change.
